criteria.reasoning: The memo connects Saffron & Sage's sole member, Celeste M. Aldana, to the director through a shared address and his annual statement naming his spouse "Celeste Aldana". It concludes that "These records strongly indicate that Saffron & Sage is wholly owned by Mr. Aldana's spouse. If confirmed, Mr. Aldana had a Financial Interest through a Family Member." It marks policy compliance as "No". That identifies an actual or possible conflict.

The memo names both failures. First: "Mr. Aldana signed on 2026-01-20 and answered 'No' to Question 2", while "Saffron & Sage's bid had been received on 2026-01-08, twelve days earlier." Second: the files contain no written disclosure from him, and the minutes record that "no other director made a disclosure" beyond Ms. Ramaswamy's.
It sets out the Article III requirement to leave the meeting and not vote. It then finds that "Mr. Aldana spoke in favor of Saffron & Sage... He moved the award of $68,400 and voted in favor."

"The motion carried 6–5... Without Mr. Aldana's vote, the count would have been 5–5. Under the bylaws, 'a tie vote fails'... the award passed only because of the vote of a director who appears to have had an undisclosed Financial Interest."

It gives Saffron & Sage's award as $68,400 and Harborview Provisions' bid as $52,900, "which the Gala Committee had recommended 3–0". It states "The Saffron & Sage bid was $15,500 above Harborview's."

Section 3 finds the policy was followed. It cites the annual statement, the written email to the Chair, the oral disclosure, her leaving the room, the ten remaining directors' conflict determination and the 10–0 approval of the lowest bid ($18,250). It concludes "No further action is required under the policy" and adds only filing and minute-keeping suggestions.

The Schedule L table answers "Report in Part IV? Yes" for Saffron & Sage on the 2025 Form 990 (fiscal year July 2025–June 2026). The reasons given are that the LLC is 100% owned by the director's apparent spouse and that $71,860 exceeds the $39,400 single-transaction threshold. The only condition is confirming the spousal identity, which the memo treats as strongly indicated, so the reporting conclusion is drawn rather than left open.
"Total revenue on the draft return is $3,940,000. One percent of that is $39,400, which is greater than $10,000. The single-transaction threshold is therefore $39,400."

BrightStage is treated as an interested person through the director's brother. Its $18,250 is tested as "Threshold (a): over $100,000 — No" and "Threshold (b): over $39,400 — No", with the result "Report in Part IV? No".

Step 2 says the committee "shall" inform him in writing of the basis for its belief and "give him an opportunity to explain... within 15 days of the notice." The memo also states "Nothing in this memo is a finding that he violated the policy."

Step 5 says the contract "shall be re-reviewed by the disinterested directors under Art. III §3(c)–(d)" with the Harborview ($52,900) and Tidewater ($55,750) bids before them. It adds that "If the re-review finds that the Theatre paid more than fair market value, the board shall consult legal counsel" on IRC §4958 and on recovery. It also notes that "The files do not establish fair market value."

Section 1 quotes Art. IV §4 and says "Mr. Aldana should not take part in the committee's discussion of Saffron & Sage." Step 1 adds that this "applies to his role as a Governance Committee member and as a director."

Step 4: "The disinterested directors, by majority, determine whether Mr. Aldana failed to disclose. If he did, the board shall take appropriate disciplinary and corrective action." Step 6: "Mr. Aldana must file a corrected statement within 30 days of the board's determination."
